claim: Assess long-duration growth quality through multi-party scuttlebutt, research productivity, sales capability, management depth and reinvestment runway.
Triangulate dated public customer, supplier, competitor and employee evidence.
Relate research investment and product cadence to economic returns.
Decline when stakeholder claims do not have independent public corroboration.
Reject long-duration quality when management depth cannot be evidenced.
Reject growth quality when research spending lacks observable product or economic output.
Excluded claim: unsourced supplier or customer claims
Excluded claim: treating reputation as evidence of growth quality
Known limit: The original scuttlebutt method relied on private conversations that this product cannot reproduce.
Known limit: Public stakeholder statements may share issuer messaging and must not be counted as independent without lineage review.
